assessment.title: Is Your Family Ready? The Legacy Readiness Check
assessment.subtitle: Ten questions, about three minutes. See what would happen to your spouse and family if something happened to you, and what's missing from your plan.
bullets: A score for documents, beneficiaries, incapacity, probate, and family readiness
A short list of what's missing, and what to do first

questions.text: Do you have a will or a living trust?

options.label: A living trust, reviewed in the last 5 years
A will, or a trust older than 5 years

questions.text: Have your documents been updated since your last big life change (move, retirement, marriage, a death, a new grandchild)?
Are the beneficiaries on your IRAs, 401(k)s and life insurance up to date?
Do your beneficiary choices match what your will or trust says?
Have you each named someone to handle finances if you can't (a durable financial power of attorney)?
Have you each named someone to make medical decisions, and written down your wishes?
If you died today, which of these would your home and main accounts go through?

options.label: A trust or beneficiary designations (no court)
Probate court, or I don't know

questions.help: Probate is the court process for settling an estate.

questions.text: Do you own real estate, including rentals or property in another state?

options.label: Yes, and it's titled to avoid probate
Yes, and I'm not sure how it's titled

questions.text: Is there anyone in your family who would need special care or protection: a child with special needs, a blended family, a family member who struggles with money?

options.label: Yes, and our plan addresses it
Yes, and our plan doesn't address it yet

questions.text: If one of you died tomorrow, would the other know where everything is and who to call first?

options.label: Yes, it's organized in one place

qualifiers.text: Roughly how much do you have saved for retirement, not counting your home?
qualifiers.help: A range is fine. It helps us point you to the right next step.

bands.label: Exposed
bands.headline: Your family isn't protected on paper yet.
bands.message: You're not alone. Most families put this off. The good news is that this is usually the fastest part of a plan to fix.

bands.label: Partly Protected
bands.headline: You've started, and there are gaps that could land on your family.
bands.message: Your focus areas below are where a gap could mean court time, delays, or hard decisions for the people you love.

bands.label: Mostly Ready
bands.headline: You're ahead of most families. A few gaps are worth closing.
bands.message: Tightening your focus areas keeps your wishes in force and your family out of the middle of it.

bands.label: Family Ready
bands.headline: Excellent. Your family is well protected on paper.
bands.message: Review your documents and beneficiaries whenever life changes, and at least every few years.

documents.low: Without a current will or trust, state law and a court decide much of what happens next.
documents.mid: You have documents. Make sure they still match your life today.
documents.high: Strong. Your core documents are in place and current.

beneficiaries.low: Beneficiary forms usually override a will. An old form can send money to the wrong person.
beneficiaries.mid: Worth a check. A beneficiary audit takes minutes and prevents expensive surprises.
beneficiaries.high: Strong. Your beneficiaries are current and consistent.

incapacity.low: If you can't make decisions and no one has legal authority, your family may need a court to appoint someone.
incapacity.mid: You're partly covered. Both spouses need both kinds of powers of attorney.
incapacity.high: Strong. Someone you trust can act for you.

court.low: Your home and accounts may have to go through probate, which takes months at minimum and is public [ATTORNEY REVIEW].
court.mid: Some assets avoid court and some may not. Titling and beneficiary deeds can close the gap.
court.high: Strong. Your assets are set up to pass without court.

family.low: A special-needs child, a blended family, or a scattered paper trail can turn a loss into a crisis. These can be planned for.
family.mid: You've thought about it. Write it down and put everything in one place your family can find.
family.high: Strong. Your family knows what to do and where to look.
